body:
Chrome MV3 allows content scripts on `file://*` when the user toggles "Allow access to file URLs" on the extension details page. This is a per-extension user toggle; we cannot script around it.

Flow:
1. Content script `content.js` (classic script, no imports, single-line IIFE after Vite's build) runs at `document_end` on every `file://` URL.
2. URL-extension check: `/\.(md|mdx|markdown)(\?[^#]*)?(#.*)?$/i`. Bail early on non-markdown files to keep Chrome's native text-file rendering as the default.
3. Chrome renders local markdown as `text/plain` inside a `<pre>`. Content script reads `document.querySelector("pre").textContent` — that's the entire raw file. No `fetch` call needed (and would be blocked by origin anyway).
4. Stash `{ url, content, name }` into `chrome.storage.session` under a fresh per-request key.
5. Redirect the tab to `chrome.runtime.getURL("src/app/index.html") + "?intercept=" + key`.
6. On the app side, `pickupIntercept()` runs after `hydrate()`, pulls the entry, materializes a one-off file in the library store, sets it active, removes the session key, cleans the URL via `history.replaceState`.

Why `chrome.storage.session` instead of passing content through URL hash? Large markdown files hit URL length limits. Session storage is per-tab-session, auto-garbage-collected when the tab closes, and handles multi-MB payloads fine. Hash-fallback exists for very old Chrome, but modern Chrome always has session storage.

Why `document_end`, not `document_start`? Need Chrome to have already rendered the text into `<pre>`. `document_start` would race the native text-file renderer.

Re-entry guard: `sessionStorage.setItem("fv-handled", url)` before the redirect. Prevents a loop if Chrome for any reason navigates back.

`web_accessible_resources` manifest entry declares `src/app/index.html` + `assets/*` as reachable from `file://`. Without this, Chrome blocks the redirect from file:// → chrome-extension:// as cross-origin.
